<p dir="auto">Agent-panel is a control panel and observability platform for optimizing and monitoring LLM/AI agents. The current version focuses on the AI gateway, providing effortless access to 100+ LLMs across 20+ AI platforms. The project is written in Rust.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Background</h2><a id="user-content-background" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Background" href="#background"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">At its core, Agent Panel addresses the complex challenges faced in managing multi-agent systems, particularly those involving numerous function-calling steps and multiple invocations.The project was born out of the difficulties faced while building and optimizing the <a href="https://github.com/IncredibleDevHQ/Incredible.dev">Incredible AI agent</a>. It highlighted the need for detailed observability of the agent's interactions, including sequential and parallel engagements with sub-agents like QnA, code search, code understanding, code generation, and evaluation agents.</p>
<p dir="auto">The initial version of Agent Panel introduces the AI Gateway, This feature alone significantly reduces the complexity and time required to connect and use different LLMs for various tasks.</p>
<p dir="auto">Here are the two significant differentiators of the agent panel.</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto">Unlike most observability tools, the agent panel takes an API-first approach rather than the wrapper approach for the OpenAI clients. It makes it easy for Vanilla implementations to integrate. In the future, I'll be building a wrapper for the OpenAI client; until then, it's more like a low-level driver and needs to be integrated using its API.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">Most observability tools track the LLM calls and their metrics but aren't designed to optimize multi-agent systems. At its core, Agent Panel addresses the complex challenges faced in managing multi-agent systems, particularly those involving numerous function-calling steps and multiple invocations.</p>
</li>
</ol>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Installation</h2><a id="user-content-installation" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Installation" href="#installation"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Build</h3><a id="user-content-build" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Build" href="#build"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">To install and run the agent-panel project, follow these steps:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Clone the repository from GitHub:</li>
</ol>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ git clone https://github.com/IncredibleDevHQ/agent-panel
$ cd agent-panel"><pre>$ git clone https://github.com/IncredibleDevHQ/agent-panel
$ <span class="pl-c1">cd</span> agent-panel</pre></div>
<ol start="2" dir="auto">
<li>Build the project using Cargo (ensure you have Rust installed on your system):</li>
</ol>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="cargo build --release"><pre>cargo build --release</pre></div>
<ol start="3" dir="auto">
<li>Create an empty config file called <code>config.yaml</code> amd Set the <code>CONFIG_DIR</code> environment variable to the directory containing your <code>config.yaml</code> file:</li>
</ol>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="export CONFIG_DIR=/path/to/directory/containing/config.yaml"><pre><span class="pl-k">export</span> CONFIG_DIR=/path/to/directory/containing/config.yaml</pre></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Configuration</h3><a id="user-content-configuration" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Configuration" href="#configuration"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">To set up the AI gateway, follow these steps:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto">Open <code>config.yaml</code> in a text editor.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">Start with an empty <code>clients:</code> section:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-yaml notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="clients:"><pre><span class="pl-ent">clients</span>:</pre></div>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">Decide which LLM platforms you want to support. You can include multiple platforms.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">For each platform you want to support, copy the relevant client configuration from the <code>example.config.yaml</code> (provided in the repo's root directory) and paste it under the <code>clients:</code> section in your <code>config.yaml</code>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Example Configuration</h3><a id="user-content-example-configuration" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Example Configuration" href="#example-configuration"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Here's an example <code>config.yaml</code> that supports both Claude and Gemini:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-yaml notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="clients:
  - type: claude
    api_key: sk-ant-xxx     # Replace with your actual Claude API key

  - type: gemini
    api_key: xxx            # Replace with your actual Gemini API key
    patches:
      '.*':                                           
        chat_completions_body:
          safetySettings:
            - category: HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT
              threshold: BLOCK_NONE
            - category: HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH
              threshold: BLOCK_NONE
            - category: HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT
              threshold: BLOCK_NONE
            - category: HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT
              threshold: BLOCK_NONE"><pre><span class="pl-ent">clients</span>:
  - <span class="pl-ent">type</span>: <span class="pl-s">claude</span>
    <span class="pl-ent">api_key</span>: <span class="pl-s">sk-ant-xxx     </span><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Replace with your actual Claude API key</span>

  - <span class="pl-ent">type</span>: <span class="pl-s">gemini</span>
    <span class="pl-ent">api_key</span>: <span class="pl-s">xxx            </span><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Replace with your actual Gemini API key</span>
    <span class="pl-ent">patches</span>:
      <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span><span class="pl-ent">.*</span><span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>:                                           
        <span class="pl-ent">chat_completions_body</span>:
          <span class="pl-ent">safetySettings</span>:
            - <span class="pl-ent">category</span>: <span class="pl-s">HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT</span>
              <span class="pl-ent">threshold</span>: <span class="pl-s">BLOCK_NONE</span>
            - <span class="pl-ent">category</span>: <span class="pl-s">HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH</span>
              <span class="pl-ent">threshold</span>: <span class="pl-s">BLOCK_NONE</span>
            - <span class="pl-ent">category</span>: <span class="pl-s">HARM_CATEGORY_SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT</span>
              <span class="pl-ent">threshold</span>: <span class="pl-s">BLOCK_NONE</span>
            - <span class="pl-ent">category</span>: <span class="pl-s">HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT</span>
              <span class="pl-ent">threshold</span>: <span class="pl-s">BLOCK_NONE</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Remember to replace the placeholder API keys with your actual credentials.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Run</h3><a id="user-content-run" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Run" href="#run"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Run the binary:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="./target/release/agent-panel"><pre>./target/release/agent-panel</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">By default, the server will run on port 8000. If you need to change the port, use the <code>--port</code> argument:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="./target/release/agent-panel --port 8080"><pre>./target/release/agent-panel --port 8080</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">This will start the server on port 8080 instead.</p>
<p dir="auto">Remember to ensure that your <code>config.yaml</code> file is properly set up with the LLM platforms you want to use before running the server.</p>
<p dir="auto">Once the server is running, you can start making requests to the AI gateway as described in the previous sections.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Develop</h3><a id="user-content-develop" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Develop" href="#develop"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">If you're developing or want to run the project without building a release version, you can use <code>cargo run</code>.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="cargo run -- [arguments]"><pre>cargo run -- [arguments]</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">For example, to run in development mode with a custom port:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="cargo run -- --port 8080"><pre>cargo run -- --port 8080</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">This will compile and run the project in one step, which is useful during development.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Using the AI Gateway</h2><a id="user-content-using-the-ai-gateway" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Using the AI Gateway" href="#using-the-ai-gateway"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">After configuring your <code>config.yaml</code>, you can start making requests to the AI gateway. Here's how to use it:</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Composing HTTP Requests</h3><a id="user-content-composing-http-requests" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Composing HTTP Requests" href="#composing-http-requests"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Endpoint URL</strong>:
Send POST requests to <code>http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions</code> (adjust if your gateway is configured differently).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Headers</strong>:
Set the Content-Type header to application/json:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="Content-Type: application/json"><pre class="notranslate"><code>Content-Type: application/json
</code></pre></div>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Request Body</strong>:
The body should be a JSON object containing:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>model</code>: Specifies which LLM to use (format: <code><platform>:<model_name></code>)</li>
<li><code>messages</code>: An array of message objects representing the conversation</li>
<li><code>stream</code>: A boolean indicating whether to stream the response (optional)</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Example cURL Request</h3><a id="user-content-example-curl-request" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Example cURL Request" href="#example-curl-request"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="curl -X POST \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "claude:claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "How does JVM work?"}],
    "stream": false
  }'"><pre>curl -X POST \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Content-Type: application/json<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  -d <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>{</span>
<span class="pl-s">    "model": "claude:claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620",</span>
<span class="pl-s">    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "How does JVM work?"}],</span>
<span class="pl-s">    "stream": false</span>
<span class="pl-s">  }<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Here's how you construct value for the "model" field in the API request.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Selecting Models</h3><a id="user-content-selecting-models" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Selecting Models" href="#selecting-models"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">When making API requests, you can only use models from platforms that you've added to your <code>config.yaml</code> file. Use the format <code><platform>:<model_name></code> in the <code>model</code> field of your HTTP request.</p>

<p dir="auto">These examples demonstrate how you can easily switch between different AI models from various platforms by simply changing the <code>model</code> field in your API requests. The AI gateway handles the routing to the appropriate platform based on the model specified.</p>
<p dir="auto">Remember that for each of these requests to work:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>The corresponding platform (OpenAI, Gemini, or Claude) must be properly configured in your <code>config.yaml</code> file.</li>
<li>You must have valid API keys for each platform.</li>
<li>The model names used in the requests must match those supported by each platform (as listed in the model table provided earlier).</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">By setting up your <code>config.yaml</code> with multiple platforms and using the appropriate model names in your requests, you can leverage the power of various AI models through a single, unified API gateway.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Roadmap</h2><a id="user-content-roadmap" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Roadmap" href="#roadmap"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The journey of Agent Panel is just beginning. The roadmap includes several exciting features designed further to enhance the capability and efficiency of AI agents:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong>Long-Term Centralized Memory:</strong> Manage and optimize the memory usage across all agents, ensuring information retention and accessibility.</li>
<li><strong>Resuming Distributed Agent State:</strong> This feature will allow the system to resume operations from the last state before a failure, preventing the need to restart processes from the beginning.</li>
<li><strong>Time Travel Debugging and Graph Visualization:</strong> Developers can step through the agent calls to debug and visualize the decision-making process, enhancing understanding and troubleshooting capabilities.</li>
<li><strong>API Function Calling Decision-Making:</strong> Rather than executing functions directly, the system will identify and suggest the best function to call based on the current context, optimizing performance and accuracy.</li>
<li><strong>Prompt Optimization Mode:</strong> This will enable developers to iterate on prompts, compare responses, and refine their strategies to achieve the best outcomes.</li>
</ol>
